title: Director at a Global Consulting Firm Sees Steady Docusign Growth Driven by IAM Expansion as eSignature Matures
expert: Strategy consultant at a global consulting firm advising mid-market to Fortune 500 clients on agreement-platform evaluation and implementation
verdict: The expert's Docusign-related consulting business rose about 3% y/y in Q3, modestly ahead of plan on IAM, with calendar 2026 seen at 5%–6% and the next quarter at only 2%–3%.

Back to double-digit growth: 🟡 **Practice up about 3% y/y** in Q3 vs +~5% and +~20% from the 2026-11-05 calls: lower.
IAM adoption: 🟢 **CLM up close to 15%** (estimate) vs 8%–10% from the 2026-11-05 consulting PMO call and Cleveland's soft CLM read (SB #63588): **conflicting**.
DBNR / renewal expansion: 🟡 **5% and 7% of renewals downgraded** (estimate); first read on downgrade rates.
🟡 **Blended pricing up around 3%** (estimate) vs +4%–5% from the 2026-11-05 AI-co exec call: slightly lower; core e-signature pressured.

changes: Practice +~3% y/y vs +~5% (2026-11-05, AI-co exec) and +~20% (2026-11-05, consulting PMO): lower.
CLM growth close to 15% (estimate) vs 8%–10% (2026-11-05, consulting PMO) and Cleveland CLM net-new deals down Y/Y (SB #63588): conflicting.
Blended pricing +~3% vs net pricing +4%–5% (2026-11-05, AI-co exec): consistent direction, lower.
First read on renewal downgrade rate (5% and 7%); no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Stance (neutral; DD growth): ↓ — CY26 5%–6% and next quarter 2%–3% (estimates), well short of double digits.
Stance (IAM bet): ↑ — IAM/AI drove the modest Q3 beat; AI contract value up to 25% in 2027 (estimate).
